title: Engagement Lighthouse Segmentation Canvas
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a lightweight, visual-first canvas to help CS managers and ICs prioritize accounts for upcoming QBRs and renewal outreach. It is intentionally heuristic — fast to apply across a book of business and adaptable for Hosted/Dedicated/Private customers.

Design principles (what we want from this sheet):
- Signal-driven: combine orthogonal signals (business value, product health, deployment nuance, contract timing) into a single priority lens.
- Actionable: each priority bucket maps to a clear engagement play (what to do, when, and who).
- Low friction: scoring should be doable from existing tooling (billing, console telemetry, support tickets) without lengthy audits.
- Audit trail: always capture the primary reason(s) an account sits in a bucket.

Core fields (one-line descriptions for the canvas):
1) Account brief (name, ARR band) — quick context.
2) ICP fit (0-4) — how closely they match our high-value use cases; 4=core ICP (AI-native, productized features), 0=mismatched.
3) Deployment mode (one of: hosted, dedicated, private) — used for friction/ops weight and SLA expectations.
4) Region impact (0-2) — whether the account spans a region where we have capacity/priority constraints.
5) Contract delta (days to renewal) — timebox: <60 / 60-180 / 180+.
6) Adoption velocity (0-5) — API calls growth, feature enablement, KV cache usage; higher = more expansion upside.
7) Health signals (0-5) — composite of SLA breaches, error rate, support tickets in 90d.
8) Cost-sensitivity flag (low/medium/high) — inferred from billing tier and usage elasticity.
9) Strategic flag (yes/no) — sales/exec-defined (e.g., marquee logos, channel partners).
10) Net priority score (computed) — weighted sum of above.
11) Recommended play (text) — high-touch cadence, renewal owner, required pre-work.
12) Rationale & next steps (notes, links) — short bullets and linked tickets.

Scoring rubric (proposal):
- ICP fit weight: 25% (score 0-4 normalized)
- Adoption velocity weight: 25% (score 0-5 normalized)
- Health signals weight: 20% (score 0-5 normalized, higher = more risk so increases priority)
- Contract proximity weight: 15% (30d buckets normalized so nearer renewals get higher weight)
- Deployment complexity weight: 10% (private/dedicated > hosted)
- Region/strategic adjustments: +/- manual offsets up to 10%

Priority buckets (thresholds are suggestions to iterate on):
- Lighthouse (score >= 0.75): immediate executive/QBR attention. Actions: 8 week renewal plan + exec sponsor, deep adoption audit, expansion proposal drafted, SLA check, pre-sales alignment.
- High-touch (0.55 - 0.75): assigned CSM weekly cadence, technical health review, deployment optimization recommendations, renewal readiness checklist.
- Maintain & Monitor (0.35 - 0.55): standard QBR cadence, automation for basic checks, focus on quick wins and feature adoption nudges.
- Watchlist / At-risk (<0.35): immediate outreach, conduct incident postmortem, escalate to solutions engineering for remedial plan.

Sample (fictional) rows to illustrate usage:
- Nimbus Data (ARR: $750k) | ICP 4 | Dedicated | Region: EU (1) | Renewal in 42d | Adoption 4 | Health 2 | Cost-sensitivity medium | Strategic yes -> Score 0.78 -> Lighthouse -> Action: schedule C-level sync, confirm SLA metrics, draft expansion bundle targeted at search-heavy workload.
- ClearVoice Labs (ARR: $120k) | ICP 3 | Hosted | Region: NA (0) | Renewal in 190d | Adoption 2 | Health 1 | Cost-sensitivity high | Strategic no -> Score 0.46 -> Maintain & Monitor -> Action: run batching/quantization recommendations, invite to optimize beta.
- Atlas Retail (ARR: $2.1M) | ICP 2 | Private | Region: APAC (2) | Renewal in 14d | Adoption 3 | Health 4 | Cost-sensitivity low | Strategic yes -> Score 0.85 -> Lighthouse -> Action: emergency health deep dive (SEs), confirm private deployment upgrade path, surface renewal terms to legal.

Playbook snippets mapped to buckets (starter templates):
- Lighthouse playbook checklist:
  - Assign exec sponsor (name/email)
  - 2-week pre-QBR: health audit, usage trend memo, demo of proposed expansion features
  - 1-week pre-QBR: legal & pricing alignment, draft renewal letter, compute impact of discount scenarios on unit economics
  - QBR agenda: 20m exec, 30m product/health, 10m pricing/next steps

- High-touch playbook checklist:
  - Weekly CSM check-ins (30m) for 8 weeks pre-renewal
  - Technical runbook: evaluate KV cache usage and request batching; recommend config tweaks
  - Customer success plan: identify 2-3 measurable adoption goals for next quarter

Open questions / notes to self (placeholders we should resolve quickly):
- How tightly do we want Health to drive priority? In practice, a major incident can spike score; should we cap the effect so the bucket doesn’t flip-flop? (suggestion: cooldown window of 14 days).
- Where to surface automation for scoring? opsconsole vs. a shared sheet. Prototype via sheet + script.
- Do we want to treat Dedicated customers with soft SRE involvement + business hours SLA differently from Private customers who need legal/renewal lead time? (likely yes).

Integration checklist (data sources for each field):
- ICP fit: account tags from CRM + manual CSM override
- Adoption velocity: API call trend (console metrics), embeddings vs gen split, new features usage (function calling, streaming)
- Health signals: incident tickets (Zendesk/Jira), runtime error rates (observability dashboard), SLA breaches (SRE logs)
- Contract delta: CRM contract end date (source of truth)
- Cost-sensitivity: billing tier, past discount history

Next steps (owners and timeline):
- Build 1-page Google Sheet prototype and test across 50 accounts (owner: Daniel Park) — target: 2024-11-15
- Sync with Solutions Eng to confirm technical data mappings (owner: Talia Nguyen) — target: 2024-11-08
- Create a Confluence page linking the canonical playbooks and attach 3 example QBR agendas (owner: Sofia Martinez) — target: 2024-11-20

Quick todo (for the initial rollout):
- [ ] Finalize weights and threshold values (CS leadership decision)
- [ ] Automate pull of adoption velocity into sheet (engineering ticket)
- [ ] Pilot with three CSMs for November QBRs

Notes / shorthand / scratchspace:
- Keep scoring granular enough to separate accounts in same ARR band; too-fine buckets hurt operational decisions.
- Early feedback suggests Sales wants Strategic flag to override scoring in some cases — record overrides with reason.
- Add a short blurb template for QBR invite emails (one-liner value props + agenda)

Appendix: quick edit-friendly QBR invite template
Subject: QBR prep — [Account name]
Body: Hi [Name], quick note to schedule our quarterly review. Agenda: 1) usage & health, 2) roadmap & product fit, 3) renewal & business outcomes. Please share any additional topics. Looking forward, [CSM name]

-- end canvas --

(Internal: file is a working draft; expect multiple iterations. Use linked_artifacts above to reference current implementation tickets and Confluence doc.)
